description:
File at https://github.com/Axect/Peroxide.

In peroxide 0.41.2, src/numerical/integral.rs, three LEGENDRE_ROOT values are wrong. Each appears twice by symmetry, so six entries.

  order 11:  0.519096129110681   should be 0.5190961292068118   (err 9.613e-11)
  order 12:  0.36783149891818    should be 0.3678314989981802   (err 8.000e-11)
  order 12:  0.125333408511469   should be 0.1252334085114689   (err 1.000e-04)

The third is the serious one and is a plain single-digit typo: a 2 became a 3 in the fourth decimal, with every remaining digit correct. It costs the 12-point rule about ten significant figures -- integrate(f, (a,b), GaussLegendre(12)) returns roughly five correct digits instead of fifteen, silently.

All the WEIGHTS are correct, at every order including 11 and 12. Only the nodes are affected.

Verification method: evaluate P_n and P_n' by Bonnet's three-term recurrence (stable at every order) and Newton-polish each tabulated node; a node that is genuinely a root does not move. All three corrections also agree with the standard published Gauss-Legendre tables to every digit. Every other value in the 928-entry table set is correct.

The harness is committed here as crates/petir/tests/gauss_legendre_table_audit.rs and is straightforward to port into a peroxide test.

Workaround per the tool's own error message: start a new session with Axect/Peroxide as the INITIAL source.

Ready-to-post draft committed at docs/upstream-issues/peroxide-gauss-legendre-nodes.md.

NOTE a reproduction correction: x^22 does NOT reproduce the bug (rel err 9.6e-16, same as corrected) because the bad node sits at x~0.125 and a high power annihilates it. Use x^2 (rel err 1.873e-05) or x^10 (2.059e-11). This is also why the bug survived in upstream, and the draft says so.

description:
PREREQUISITE for op-v5zb. We know 1:1 with wall time is structurally unreachable (fixed sleep after compute); we do NOT know by how much. Measure before choosing a fix.

Cheapest read, no new code: time the existing test

  cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --examples \
    the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep

It advances 20 000 steps at 1 ms = 20 s of simulated time through HtgrPlant::step, the same call the GUI physics thread makes. Wall seconds / 20 = the compute-only real-time ratio, excluding the 10 ms sleep. Then the achieved GUI ratio is 10/(10 + 10*per_step_ms).

Also worth splitting out, since it decides which fix is right: how much of the per-step cost is the steam generator. SteamGeneratorConfig::substep is 0.0125 s and the exchanger accumulates, so only ~0.8 array advances land per 10 ms tick -- the three coupled arrays may be a spike every 12-13 substeps rather than a uniform cost. Time HtgrPlant::step with and without a whole SG advance falling inside it.

Record the measured numbers in the bead and in the doc comment per the workspace V&V rule. Do not fix anything under this bead.

notes.content:
DONE 2026-08-13. Measured via the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep, release, 20,000 steps of 1 ms:
  41.79 s quiescent, 49.00 s contended => 2.09-2.45 ms of COMPUTE per 1 ms of PLANT time.
  Real-time ratio: 0.29-0.32 under the old fixed-sleep scheme; 0.41-0.48 after deadline pacing landed.
Conclusion: pacing alone cannot reach 1:1; the physics is ~2.2x too expensive at dt = 1 ms. This is what motivated
the global 0.1 s timestep bead. NOTE the 20 percent duty figure recorded in op-szmi.16 predates the nodalised steam
generator (edbb2bd7) and is off by roughly 12x -- do not cite it.

description:
Source: https://github.com/Adolphus8/Transitional_Ensemble_MCMC (MATLAB, GPL-3.0 by grant).

Transitional Markov Chain Monte Carlo -- the workhorse sampler for Bayesian model
updating, and the highest-value single item in this epic. Handles multimodal and
poorly-scaled posteriors where plain Metropolis-Hastings stalls, by annealing
through a sequence of intermediate distributions.

Cite the MATLAB source file and commit in the doc comment so the two cannot
drift unnoticed. V&V per the workspace rule: methodology AND measured results --
recover a known posterior analytically where one exists.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
LANDED IN SUBSTANCE, not as a literal port, verified 2026-09-17: crates/raffles/src/bayesian/transitional.rs implements TMCMC (Ching & Chen 2007) and TEMCMC (Lye/Cicirello/Patelli 2021/2022) as one tempering driver, with adaptive tempering by bisection on the weight CoV, systematic resampling and log-evidence. Verified against closed-form posteriors (conjugate Normal-Normal, Occam factor, Himmelblau's four peaks) AND cross-checked against upstream TEMCMCsampler.m/TMCMCsampler.m run under Octave (crates/raffles/docs/cross-check-against-upstream.md) -- TEMCMC agrees to under 1 SE over 5 seeds.

DIVERGES from the literal instruction: not transcribed from Transitional_Ensemble_MCMC (no LICENSE file on that repo at the time), written from the cited papers instead -- see op-dwqw.1. Also: this crate's own docs record it has NO adaptive proposal scaling where the author's MATLAB does (finding F3), a real gap left to the owner's call. Not closing -- flagging for Adolphus Lye's review given the port-vs-independent-implementation divergence.

design:
Child epic of the integrated petrochemical and polymer platform (bn op-9941 / see #77 programme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model**

**A separate chemistry family. This is not an LHHW catalytic reactor** — it is
primarily homogeneous free-radical thermal cracking, and reusing the catalytic
path would be modelling the wrong physics.

**Feeds** eventually: ethane; propane; LPG; naphtha; potentially heavier.

**Products**: H2; methane; ethylene; propylene; acetylene; C4s; butadiene;
pyrolysis gasoline; heavier pyrolysis products; coke.

Initial model may use literature-supported **lumped kinetics**; detailed radical
mechanisms are future fidelity.

## HTGR relevance — this is the flagship high-temperature integration

```
HTGR -> high-temperature intermediate loop -> cracker furnace / process heater
     -> cracking coils
```

**Do not assume direct primary-helium contact with hydrocarbons.** The
intermediate loop is not optional detail; it is the safety architecture.

Cracking is the highest-temperature sink in the complex and therefore the
strongest case for nuclear process heat — which makes getting its temperature
level right in the heat ledger particularly important.


## Programme constraints

No monolithic plant solvers. Reuse existing reaction/thermo/separation infrastructure. Conservation preserved across every representation change. Do not push to `main`.
title: Petchem: Steam / naphtha cracking

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-10 (session_01AhE6XBx3nRd81aHLQrciQe): FIRST GOLDEN-FILE VALIDATION of the ported GROUPR engine against a real NJOY2016 GENDF tape - the "top V&V ask" of op-3ut/op-cpz/op-ini is now measured, for the vector (mfd=3) path with the Bondarenko self-shielded flux (nsigz>1).

Oracle: NJOY2016 ac5adf5 (2016.79) built in-session; RECONR(0.001)/BROADR(293.6 K)/GROUPR on ENDF/B-VIII.0 U-238 (MAT 9237), ign=1 (29 user groups 1e-5..2e7 eV), iwt=3 (1/E), lord=0, sigz = 1e10 1e4 1e3 1e2 10 1, MT 1/2/18/102. Golden GENDF (35 KB) + the exact deck committed at reference-data/gendf/ (README with provenance); new accessor reference_data::reference_file("gendf", ..) (+ OUTRAM_PARK_REFERENCE_DATA_DIR override). Test: crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/tests/groupr_u238_gendf_golden.rs (methodology + results in its doc comment).

Upstream read before measuring: getwtf iwt=3 -> wtf=1/e, enext=1.01*e (groupr.f90:5203); genflx nsigz>1 tabulates wtf*(sigpot+sigz)/(sigt+sigz) on the greedy union of 1% steps and the MT=1 grid (:5623-5665), getflx interpolates it lin-lin (:6478-6490); sigpot=0 unless iwt<0 (:4978); lord=0 with nsigz>1 promotes MT=1 to NL=2 (P0+P1, :6498-6499), other MTs stay NL=1; panel = trapezoid flux + rate-linear-across-panel (:5858-6091) == our group_integral. Prediction stated before measuring: <1e-5 with NJOY's own PENDF, O(1e-3) with the crate's RECONR/BROADR.

MEASURED (all 29 groups x 6 sigma0):
 Tier 1, engine isolated on NJOY's own PENDF (env OUTRAM_PARK_NJOY_U238_PENDF; 155,207 sigt points -> 156,864 flux points, NJOY listing: 156,854): max |dsigma_g/sigma_g| = 6.85e-7 (MT=1), 4.55e-7 (MT=2), 2.07e-6 (MT=18), 2.65e-6 (MT=102, group 9, sigma0=inf); max group-flux dev 4.93e-7 (= the 7-significant-figure storage floor). PASS at 1e-5. The group-averaging engine (genflx_bondarenko + panel/group_integral + self_shielded_group_xs) reproduces NJOY.
 Tier 2, crate RECONR(0.001)+BROADR(293.6 K) from the committed ENDF tape (961,139 sigt points; 156 s): max dev 1.98e-4 (MT=1), 1.98e-4 (MT=2), 9.24e-4 (MT=102), flux 6.06e-5 -> PASS at 3e-3. MT=18 1.14e-2 (group 13, 40-50 eV, sigma_f ~2.5e-7 b). Read upstream: reconr.f90:109-117, 428-430 - where a point's resonance-integral contribution is below errint = err/20000 = 5e-8 b, NJOY converges it only to errmax = 10*err = 1 % (NJOY listing: 363,092 points "affected by resonance integral check"). Sub-threshold U-238 fission sits entirely under that floor, so the 1.1 % is NJOY's own linearization slack, not an engine defect (tier 1 shows 2e-6 on MT=18 with NJOY's grid). Asserted at 3e-2 for MT=18, 3e-3 otherwise.

NOT covered (still open): the matrix path (mfd=6 scatter matrices, File-6 feeds, op-ini's port half), URR self-shielding via MT=152 (no UNRESR step in this deck - op-cpz's read_urr_table half), GAMINR, lord>0.

Side findings (filed separately): crate RECONR lacks the errint/errmax resonance-integral relaxation (961k vs NJOY 448k points at the same err); crate BROADR does no thinning (NJOY 448,168 -> 155,207 at errthn=0.001).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-14 bookkeeping reconciliation. Nearly every gap this bead names has closed, most of it on 2026-09-13/14, after the bead's last update.

CLOSED:
- getmf6 File-6 continuum feed (groupr.f90:6521-8133) -- ported as src/groupr/mf6_feed.rs + mf6_feed/{records,tests}.rs (commit 932819a51), then WIRED into the matrix driver as Continuum6Feed behind the GroupFeed trait (5bbac8a82). The same commit fixed f6lab dropping every feed's first panel -- a real defect the port had, found by wiring it.
- f6lab (9063-9338), ll2lab (8934-9061), f6dis (8719-8810) -- ported 2026-09-13 (7e850615d), which also verified the pass the original translator could not run.
- File-4 anisotropic angular distributions -- getfle (9679-9873) and getco (10462-10705) are ported in src/groupr/file4.rs, incl. LTT=1/2/3 and NJOY's own 64-point Gauss-Legendre node/weight tables; the exact getdis is src/groupr/two_body.rs::TwoBodyFeed driven by matrix_panel::two_body_matrix.
- 'the top V&V ask is a golden-file comparison of any ported matrix vs a real NJOY GROUPR GENDF tape (none of op-3ut is validated against NJOY output yet)' -- this is NO LONGER TRUE. There are now five committed GROUPR goldens against NJOY2016 ac5adf5 tapes, two of them matrix: tests/groupr_u238_elastic_matrix_golden.rs (elastic P0-P3), tests/groupr_u238_inelastic_matrix_golden.rs (discrete inelastic MT 51/52/60/89), plus groupr_u238_gendf_golden.rs (vector, 29g x 6 sigma0), groupr_u238_derived_quantities_golden.rs (MT 257-259) and groupr_u235_mf10_golden.rs (2.2e-6). Write-up: verification_and_validation/groupr_gaminr_covr_leapr_vs_njoy2016.md.

GENUINELY still open:
- getaed heating (9874-10239) -- absent; the only two hits in src/ are module-map mentions in groupr/README.md and groupr/mod.rs.
- MF=6 LAW=6 (n-body phase space, needs f6psp), LAW=2..5 and LAW=-4 via getdis mft=8, and the disc102 relativistic capture gamma -- all still NotPorted in mf6_feed.rs and documented there line-by-line against upstream.
- the iwt=0/1/-3 flux-calculator card branches (groupr/input.rs card8a/8b/8d) still refuse rather than fabricate.

Doc drift fixed in the same pass: groupr/matrix.rs's FeedFunction::AnisotropicElastic and ::Continuum6 both carried '**not ported**' docs. Both are now superseded PLACEHOLDERS on an older isotropic-only surface -- the real feeds are ported and wired elsewhere -- and a reader of that enum would have concluded GROUPR still cannot do continuum or anisotropic feeds. Neither variant is constructed anywhere outside matrix.rs's own test; docs corrected to point at the real drivers, behaviour (NotPorted rather than a silently wrong answer) deliberately unchanged.

Suggest RETITLING to the getaed + MF=6 LAW=2..6 remainder. Not closed here; closing is the maintainer's call.
